summary: poc-revshell spawns reverse shell on pip install and on import
details: poc-revshell 0.1.0 ships a reverse-shell backdoor that fires both at install time and at import time. setup.py registers a custom `install` cmdclass (PostInstall) that starts a daemon thread executing a routine which opens a TCP socket to 127.0.0.1:4444, dup2s the socket file descriptor onto stdin/stdout/stderr, and execs `/bin/sh -i` (or `cmd.exe` on Windows); this runs automatically during `pip install`. The package's `__init__.py` contains the same thread-launch at module top level, so every `import poc_revshell` repeats the handoff. Any local listener on port 4444 at the moment of install or import receives a full interactive shell running under the installing user's identity. The destination is hardcoded loopback, which confines the attack to a co-resident attacker on the installer's host, but the install-time and import-time network-to-shell dataflow is a backdoor by structure, matching the package's self-description as a proof-of-concept that triggers a reverse shell on pip install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
